summary: DIRECTER couples KV-cache key scaling with a plausibility-guided decoding loop and an attention-sensitivity layer ranking to adaptively modulate steering strength and mitigate oversteering. The method is a sensible, genuinely useful combination of existing ideas (contrastive/plausibility decoding + activation steering) that consistently beats zero-shot and prior steering baselines (PASTA, SpotLight) across five models and three benchmarks while preserving text quality and task fidelity. The gains are moderate (≈6.5 points over zero-shot, ≈4 over tuned steering baselines) and the empirical case is weakened by absent error bars/significance tests on the main results and reliance on an LLM judge, but the ablations, efficiency analysis, and modular safety-gate result make this a competent borderline-accept submission.
strengths: Tackles a real and well-motivated problem (oversteering in activation steering) with an adaptive, per-step control mechanism rather than static hyperparameters, which is a meaningful conceptual improvement over PASTA/SpotLight.
The plausibility filter is shown to be modular: applied as a safety gate it also improves PASTA and SpotLight (Fig 2b), supporting the generality claim and adding value beyond the single method.

Reasonable experimental breadth: five models spanning 1B–14B across two families, three benchmarks, plus targeted ablations (ranking reversed, random layers, random tokens) that isolate the key design choices.

Fairness and calibration are good: DIRECTER uses a single fixed (α, β) across all tasks while baselines get per-method tuning, and limitations (no theoretical grounding for the sensitivity metric, cleanly-separated task/instruction assumption) are stated openly.
Practicality is addressed: efficiency analysis (≈16% throughput reduction, negligible memory, FlashAttention compatibility) makes the method deployable, unlike some attention-level interventions.

key_concerns.issue: Main results (Tables 1, 2, 4) report single point estimates with no error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests; only two ablation rows carry ±std. Greedy decoding removes per-run stochasticity but not benchmark-sampling variance, so it is hard to know whether a ~4-point gap over tuned SpotLight is statistically real.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report variance across multiple seeds/prompt variants or bootstrap confidence intervals over benchmark items, and add significance tests for the headline comparisons against the strongest tuned baselines.

key_concerns.issue: Text-quality and task-fidelity claims (Table 4, ≈92% fidelity) rest primarily on a gpt-4o-mini judge, and IFEval prompts were themselves rewritten with gpt-4o-mini, raising judge-bias and evaluation-circularity concerns. The corroborating human evaluation is deferred to an appendix with unspecified scale/agreement.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move the human evaluation protocol (number of annotators, items, inter-annotator agreement) into the main text, and report judge robustness with at least one alternative judge model.

key_concerns.issue: GSM8K-Format is an author-designed benchmark; without releasing exact construction rules and difficulty distribution it is hard to rule out favorable design, and it drives one of the strongest headline contrasts (PASTA task accuracy collapse 82.7→62.7).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Fully specify the GSM8K-Format construction and, if possible, validate the oversteering-vs-task-accuracy trade-off on an independently constructed formatting benchmark.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is incremental: plausibility-guided decoding (Li et al. 2022; Chuang et al. 2023) and KV-cache steering are pre-existing; the contribution is their combination plus the sensitivity ranking. The α=100 key-scaling regime is unusual and its interaction with softmax renormalization deserves more analysis.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen the delineation from contrastive/DoLa-style decoding in Related Work and add a short analysis of why extreme key scaling behaves stably (the α-saturation result in Fig 3b is a good start but should be explained mechanistically).

questions_for_authors: Can you provide variance/significance for the main-table comparisons, given that the DIRECTER-vs-tuned-SpotLight gap on several columns is only a few points?
How sensitive are the Table 4 quality/fidelity conclusions to the choice of LLM judge, and what were the human-eval sample size and inter-annotator agreement?
Since IFEval prompts were rewritten with gpt-4o-mini to separate task/instruction spans, how much of the reported gain depends on this preprocessing versus the steering mechanism itself?
What is the wall-clock cost and accuracy under the automatic span-detection setting (Appendix D.2) when tasks and instructions are not cleanly separable, i.e., the realistic case?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well scoped—'up to 6.5%', explicit trade-off preservation, and stated limitations—though 'general mechanism' and 'model-agnostic' phrasing slightly outrun the English-only, ≤14B, two-family evidence.

significance.justification: Oversteering mitigation and adaptive per-step steering are useful contributions to an active subfield, and the modular safety-gate result broadens impact, though the gains are moderate rather than field-changing.

novelty.justification: A genuinely useful new mechanism, but assembled from existing components (plausibility/contrastive decoding, KV-cache steering) rather than a fundamentally new idea.

rigor.justification: Method is sound and ablations isolate ranking, layer selection, and token selection, but the claim–evidence link on the main results is weakened by absent variance reporting.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main tables give single numbers with no error bars or significance tests; only two ablation rows report std, so small margins over tuned baselines are not shown to be reliable.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations are stated candidly (no theory for the metric, clean-span assumption), gains are hedged as 'up to 6.5%', though generality wording is mildly overstated.

clarity.justification: Method, algorithm, and RQ structure are followable and the plausibility loop is well explained; some equation-level details are dense and rely on appendices.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure is present and well used (RQ-driven experiments, ablations, efficiency, qualitative examples), within reasonable length.

reproducibility.justification: Models, fixed hyperparameters (α=100, β=0.5), decoding setup, and the algorithm are specified; several key details (span detection, GSM8K-Format construction, human-eval protocol) are relegated to appendices.

related_work.justification: Positioning against PASTA and SpotLight is fair and specific, but differentiation from contrastive/DoLa-style plausibility decoding is thin given how central that idea is to the method.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-supporting displays (overview loop, fixed-strength ablation, compatibility, robustness sweeps, efficiency), adequate to convey the results.

breadth_generality.justification: Five models across two families and three benchmarks support the core claims, but generality is limited to English, ≤14B, cleanly separated task/instruction settings, so broad 'general-purpose' claims are only partly backed.

overall_recommendation.justification: A competent, useful borderline-accept contribution whose moderate gains and thin statistical reporting keep it just above the typical ICLR bar rather than clearly over it.
